searchText: I do admit that original intention of ACCEPTED was to reflect Erigon's behaviour, i.e. exactly how Danny has described it. Then at some point I messed up with the semantics of ACCEPTED hence my confusion (and probably not only mine). We can align the spec to this original intention and have ACCEPTED and SYNCING statuses in response to `newPayload` -- I am pretty fine with this. I was thinking about potential use case for ACCEPTED on CL side. CL may leverage it in the following way: it does poll `fcU` if it knows that a chain of ACCEPTED blocks has a common ancestor that isn't that far from current head and expected time to execute this chain is relatively low. Though, not sure if it's valuable for CL to have this kind of logic around ACCEPTED. I am also curious does Erigon check things not related to execution e.g. gasLimit, baseFee before returning ACCEPTED? cc <@583892532644151312> On another topic. excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
I do admit that original intention of ACCEPTED was to reflect Erigon's behaviour, i.e. exactly how Danny has described it. Then at some point I messed up with the semantics of ACCEPTED hence my confusion (and probably not only mine).

We can align the spec to this original intention and have ACCEPTED and SYNCING statuses in response to `newPayload` -- I am pretty fine with this.

I was thinking about potential use case for ACCEPTED on CL side. CL may leverage it in the following way: it does poll `fcU` if it knows that a chain of ACCEPTED blocks has a common ancestor that isn't that far from current head and expected time to execute this chain is relatively low. Though, not sure if it's valuable for CL to have this kind of logic around ACCEPTED.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: I am also curious does Erigon check things not related to execution e.g. gasLimit, baseFee before returning ACCEPTED? cc <@583892532644151312>

On another topic. There is an idea to make EL validate that `finalized`, `safe` and `head` do belong to the same chain. How big of implementation complexity it would be for your EL client? Related to this convo: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/213#discussion_r862153230

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
Are you looking into execution payload deduplication? There is still an open PR on this topic https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/146
with related discussion thread https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/137

You might want to champion this or a similar proposal. I think that `eth_getBlockByHash` isn't a good solution for deduplication as it doesn't support batching and might be more resourceful for EL to process. Also, as you have mentioned it may not be supported during sync, while we can design `engine_` method with more liberty considering trustful relationships between CL and EL
